body: how to you get the result? It is not part of the commands above...
have you tried turning off the schema cache? just reproduced the issue btw.
@cebe Ofcourse ;-) Btw FYI schema cache not used for such low level operations and that layer.

@cebe I assume this trouble caused by wrong PDO usage and prepared statement. Most interesting thing is if you kill first insert everything will be fine with second insert. So bug is very funny. On other side its extremally dangerous especially for production environment. For example consider you have 4 migrations: 1) create table, 2) insert into that table, 3) alter table, 4) insert into that table. On dev environment you'll run migrations step by step and you'll get one result. When you run `yii migrate` on production and all migrations in one step you'll be very surprised.

**Note:** its pure Yii 2 DAO layer bug. Implemeting same using PDO and 2 prepared statements work as expected.

It is the schema cache, add the following after alterColumn and it will work:

``` php
$this->db->schema->getTableSchema('testAlterTable', true); // true = refresh
```
@cebe Again, it not schema cache :) I specially double check that it is disabled inside config.
@cebe As i said before. If you kill first insert, second will work as expected. So trouble is VERY COMPLEX. Adding additional commands after of before something affect result.

The problem is the dbCast call in insert method of QueryBuilder.

this line:
https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/master/framework/db/QueryBuilder.php#L151
which calls the typecast function and here you turn your `'hello'` into `0`:
https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/master/framework/db/ColumnSchema.php#L134

It is not the cache itself but the tableschema is cached per request.
make a step debug with xdebug on the second insert call and you will see it cast to int there.

> If you kill first insert, second will work as expected.

Yes, because it will not have loaded table schema yet.
